advocate.load_bearing_assumption: The assumption that India and Bangladesh must negotiate and sign a brand-new, complex successor treaty rather than a simple, stop-gap bilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to temporarily extend or govern water sharing beyond the 2026 expiration.
advocate.why_it_could_be_wrong: To avoid a dangerous legal and operational vacuum on January 1, 2027, both nations have a massive mutual incentive to sign a basic, temporary MoU extending the 1996 terms. The resolution criteria explicitly allow for a 'memorandum of understanding... that explicitly governs the sharing of Ganga water beyond the expiration,' which is vastly easier and faster to sign than a full treaty, bypassing the lengthy Joint Rivers Commission technical reviews and domestic state-level (West Bengal) blockages.
advocate.move_reason: The current aggregate of 38.0% overweights the structural and political difficulty of negotiating a brand-new treaty under tight timelines (132 days remaining), while underestimating the high probability of a stop-gap MoU. Because the resolution criteria explicitly include an MoU governing sharing beyond the expiration, the bar for success is lower than a full treaty ratification, justifying a shift upward closer to even odds.
advocate.concerns: The extremely short timeline (132 days) combined with the ongoing political transition and volatility in Bangladesh means even a simple MoU could be delayed by bureaucratic paralysis or anti-India sentiment in Dhaka, making any forecast above 50% too risky.
